# A Hausdorff-measure normal-cone injection outside a projected cylinder

This is an explicit finite-translation lemma. It preserves the actual
mixed-integer lattice when used on mixed-integer sets, treats ties with
positive measure, and requires no limit of output bodies or halfspaces.
It extends the mechanism in
`candidate 669694f08be75bf9`.
It is not a selection theorem for OC.

## 1. Statement

Let A,B be nonempty compact subsets of R^m. Let V be a linear subspace,
W=V^perp, and pi the orthogonal projection onto W. Put

    P=pi(conv B),       Z=pi^(-1)(P)=V+conv B.

For q>=0 suppose H_q(A)<infinity. Let E be a Borel subset of A,
and suppose a fixed Borel set H contains E+B. Then

    H_q(((A+B) intersect H) minus Z)>=H_q(E minus V).       (1)

In particular, for a closed halfspace it suffices to require the
readily checked stronger condition

    H={x:ell(x)>=beta},
    ell(a)>=beta-min_(b in B)ell(b) for every a in E.       (2)

When V=R^m the right side is zero, so the statement is trivial. The
meaningful proof below assumes W has positive dimension. Empty E
also gives a trivial inequality. The q=0 measure is counting measure;
the proof does not discard a point or a tie on the basis of an
inapplicable null-boundary assertion.

## 2. Approximate only the supporting points

For epsilon>0 let

    E_epsilon={a in E:||pi a||>=epsilon}.

Choose a finite set F subset B whose projected convex hull P_F
satisfies

    0<=h_P(v)-h_(P_F)(v)<=delta||v|| for every v in W,
    0<delta<epsilon.                                      (3)

Such an F exists: choose a finite delta-net of the compact set B,
using actual points of B. Every convex combination is approximated
by the corresponding convex combination of the chosen points with
error at most delta; orthogonal projection does not increase the
error. Comparing scalar products gives (3).

List the distinct vertices p_1,...,p_N of P_F and choose one fixed
actual lift b_i in F with pi b_i=p_i. A vertex of a finite convex
hull is one of its generating projected points, so these lifts exist.
This includes lower-dimensional P_F and its singleton case.

For each v in W choose the SMALLEST index i maximizing v.p_i.
Its decision regions are Borel sets, described by finitely many
strict or weak linear inequalities. In particular they partition
ALL of W, including every tie hyperplane. Define

    Phi_epsilon(a)=a+b_(i(pi a)),    a in E_epsilon.       (4)

Every image point belongs to A+B and to H by the assumed inclusion
E+B subset H. No convexification of A or of its target is used.

## 3. Original-cylinder avoidance and injectivity

Put v=pi a. At the selected vertex, (3) gives

    v.pi(Phi_epsilon(a))
       =||v||^2+h_(P_F)(v)
       >=h_P(v)+||v||(||v||-delta)>h_P(v).                 (5)

Thus the image avoids the ORIGINAL closed cylinder Z, not merely
the one built from the finite approximation. The strict gap is
provided by ||v||>=epsilon>delta. No limiting output point can erase
this gap, since no limit of output points is being taken.

The map is injective. For any selected vertices p_i at v and p_j
at w, the two maximizing inequalities, even in the presence of ties,
imply

    (v-w).(p_i-p_j)>=0.                                  (6)

If Phi_epsilon(a)=Phi_epsilon(a'), projecting gives
v-w=p_j-p_i. Substitution in (6) yields
-||p_i-p_j||^2>=0, so p_i=p_j. The list of projected vertices is
distinct and uses one lift per vertex, hence i=j and b_i=b_j.
The original equality now gives a=a'.

Partition E_epsilon into its finitely many decision pieces. On each
piece (4) is one actual translation, preserving H_q. The images are
Borel, pairwise disjoint by injectivity, and lie in the left-hand
set of (1). Countable additivity of Hausdorff measure on Borel sets
therefore gives

    H_q(((A+B) intersect H) minus Z)>=H_q(E_epsilon).       (7)

For epsilon=1/j these source sets increase to E minus V. Continuity
from below of the same measure proves (1). This is the only limit
in the proof. It varies no body, fiber, normal, chosen center, or
halfspace, and does not require convergence of the maps (4).

## 4. Mixed-integer and intrinsic-measure versions

If A,B subset Lambda=Z^n times R^d in R^m, m=n+d, every selected
b_i belongs to Lambda. Addition by b_i preserves Lambda exactly,
and hence every image in (4) is an actual mixed-integer sum point.
Hausdorff measure is invariant under these translations for every q;
there is no determinant or ambient-volume substitution. Thus (1)
holds verbatim for H_q on these sets, including q=0 and lower-
dimensional fibers. The explicit subtraction of E intersect V is
retained when that subspace carries positive H_q measure.

For q=d, bounded measurable subsets of Lambda have finitely many
fibers and H_d equals the sum of their d-dimensional volumes. Thus
the same result is also an exact mixed-integer-volume statement.
For q=0, H_0(A)<infinity forces A finite; ties and points on V are
handled by precisely the same deterministic partition and subtraction.

No assertion is made that (A+B)/2 is mixed-integer unless its integer
coordinates are known to be even. If A and B have one common integer
parity class, this additional property DOES hold, and a midpoint
application may use it while retaining its actual H_q scaling 2^-q.
No replacement of that factor by Gamma_d is justified by this lemma.

## 5. The all-dimensional far-tail reserve as a corollary

Let A,B be d-dimensional convex bodies, d>=2, and let S subset A
be a segment lying in an affine line a_0+V. Translate A and S by
-a_0, leave B fixed, and translate the tested halfspace by -a_0;
then V is linear. Suppose the original far-tail set E subset A has
E+B inside the tested halfspace. Apply (1) to its translated version.
The line V has d-dimensional measure zero, so the right side is
|E|. Moreover S+B subset V+conv B. Thus the disjoint target
provided by (1) lies outside S+B. Since S+B subset A+B,

    |(A+B) intersect H|-|(S+B) intersect H|>=|E|.           (8)

Taking E=A intersect {t>=c}, min_B t>=-c and H={t>=0}
recovers the additive reserve. This proof needs no polynomial body
approximation and no assumption about the target cap boundary having
zero measure. For d=1 the line is the full space and H_1(E minus V)
is zero, exactly identifying why the stronger far-tail conclusion
does not hold in that dimension.

The same argument applies to any affine subspace of dimension less
than q, provided the source Hausdorff measure is finite and the
actual E+B halfspace inclusion holds. If the subspace has positive
source measure, the exact residual H_q(E minus V) must remain.

## 6. An additive reserve for a common residual hull

Use the setting of
`candidate 5dd69a77cceb0773`.
Let J have k actual residual regions with 2<=k<=d, let P be their
one common hull of dimension r=k-1, and put

    E=A intersect intersection_(i notin J){v_i.x<-1},
    G=intersection_(i notin J){v_i.x<0}.

These are Borel sets, E+B subset G, and P+B subset G. Translate
P's affine span to a linear subspace as in Section5. Since r<d,
that span has zero d-volume. The finite translation argument and
source-set continuity therefore give added volume at least |E| inside
(A+B) intersect G and outside aff(P)+conv B, in particular outside
P+B. No single limiting map on all E is asserted. It follows that

    |(A+B) intersect G|>=|P+B|+|E|>2^(k-1)b+|E|.

The strict inequality is exactly the independently proved common-hull
bound. As G is defined by homogeneous linear inequalities and
(A+B)/2 subset K, division by2 yields

    2^d |K intersect G|>2^(k-1)b+|E|.                (9)

This is one swept-hull set plus the disjoint added-volume lower bound.
It does not sum overlapping pairwise hulls or several independently
injected copies. In the planar case k=2, if u is the A cap mass in the sole
remaining normal, then |E|=a-u and (9) becomes

    |K intersect {v_small.x<0}|>b/2+(a-u)/4.

No k=d+1 extension of this extra term is claimed: the affine span
is then the whole space and its source measure cannot be discarded.
